items.topic: Oral iron — best absorbed empty stomach; separate from milk/calcium/antacids; vitamin C enhances
items.stem: The nurse teaches a client starting oral ferrous sulfate for iron-deficiency anemia. Which instruction is correct?

options.text: Take on an empty stomach if tolerated; avoid taking with milk, calcium, or antacids; vitamin C (e.g., orange juice) can enhance absorption
Always crush the tablet into a glass of milk at bedtime for best absorption
Take with a calcium antacid every dose to protect the stomach and improve absorption
Stop the supplement if stools turn black because black stools always mean gastrointestinal bleeding

rationales.A: Correct. MedlinePlus: iron best absorbed on empty stomach; separate milk/calcium/antacids (≥2 hours); vitamin C/orange juice can help absorption. Merck: absorbed best empty stomach; antacids/calcium reduce absorption; vitamin C enhances; black stools are a harmless side effect.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Milk/calcium impair absorption; bedtime-with-milk is not preferred teaching.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Antacids and calcium reduce iron absorption.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Black stools are expected with oral iron; tarry stools with red streaks or severe pain warrant provider contact.

items.topic: NGN cloze — oral iron absorption helpers and expected black stools
items.stem: Complete the teaching for oral iron therapy.

ngn.template: Iron is often absorbed better when taken with {B1}, and clients should be told that {B2} while taking iron tablets.

B1.text: milk or a calcium antacid at the same time
vitamin C (for example orange juice) if recommended
high-fiber bran cereal in the same swallow

B2.text: black stools are expected and usually harmless
black stools always require an emergency colonoscopy the same day
stool colour never changes with iron therapy

rationales.B1b: Correct. Vitamin C/orange juice can enhance absorption (MedlinePlus/Merck).
rationales.B1c: Incorrect. High-fiber foods can impair concurrent absorption.
rationales.B2a: Correct. Black stools are a normal, harmless effect of oral iron.
rationales.B2b: Incorrect. Black stools alone are expected; urgent evaluation is for tarry stools with red streaks or severe pain.
rationales.B2c: Incorrect. Stool colour commonly turns black with oral iron.

items.topic: Artificial nails — do not wear for high-risk direct care; keep natural nails short
items.client_needs_subcategory: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
items.stem: A nurse is assigned to direct care in an intensive care unit. Which fingernail practice is appropriate?

options.text: Keep natural nails short (not extending past the fingertip) and do not wear artificial nails or extensions for this high-risk direct care
Wear long acrylic nails because alcohol hand rub always sterilizes under artificial nails
Grow natural nails well past the fingertip to protect the nail bed during glove use
Apply gel nail enhancements for every shift because they improve hand hygiene effectiveness

rationales.A: Correct. CDC: natural nails should not extend past the fingertip; do not wear artificial nails/extensions when having direct contact with high-risk patients (e.g., ICU/OR). PHO PIDAC: keep natural nails clean and short (not past fingertip); artificial nails/enhancements must not be worn for direct client care.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Germs can persist under artificial nails even after hand hygiene; CDC/PHO advise against artificial nails in high-risk/direct care.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Long nails harbour more organisms and are harder to clean.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Nail enhancements are not recommended for direct care hand hygiene effectiveness.

items.topic: Food thermometer — only reliable way to confirm safe internal cooking temperature
items.stem: A community health nurse teaches safe home cooking. Which statement shows correct understanding?

options.text: Use a food thermometer to check that meat and poultry reach a safe internal temperature; colour alone is not a reliable doneness guide
If ground beef looks brown in the middle, it is always safe without checking temperature
A food thermometer is unnecessary if the outside of poultry looks crispy
Guessing doneness by smell is as accurate as a thermometer for leftovers

rationales.A: Correct. CDC: only way to tell if food is safely cooked is a food thermometer; colour/texture (except seafood) are unreliable. Health Canada: use a food thermometer in the thickest part to verify safe cooking temperatures.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Colour alone does not confirm a safe internal temperature.
rationales.C: Incorrect. External appearance does not replace thermometer verification.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Smell is not a substitute for measured internal temperature.

items.topic: Secondhand smoke — no safe level; smoke-free home and car; fans do not eliminate risk
items.stem: A nurse teaches a family about protecting children from secondhand tobacco smoke. Which teaching is correct?

options.text: There is no safe level of secondhand smoke; make the home and car smoke-free because opening windows or using fans does not eliminate the risk
Smoking in a bedroom with the door closed fully protects children elsewhere in the home
A kitchen fan removes all secondhand smoke toxins within minutes
Brief exposure to secondhand smoke is always harmless for infants

rationales.A: Correct. CDC: no safe level; eliminate smoking; do not smoke in home/car; fans/windows/air purifiers do not get rid of secondhand smoke. Health Canada: no safe level; make home and car smoke-free; fans/windows/air fresheners do not completely eliminate toxins.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Smoke spreads through the home even from another room.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Ventilation/fans do not eliminate secondhand smoke risk.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Even brief exposure can harm; children are especially vulnerable.

items.topic: Umbilical cord stump — keep clean and dry; fold diaper below; do not pull off
items.stem: The nurse teaches parents about care of the newborn umbilical cord stump. Which instruction is correct?

options.text: Keep the stump clean and dry, fold the diaper below the stump, sponge bathe until it falls off naturally, and do not pull it off
Pull the stump off as soon as it looks loose to speed healing
Cover the stump tightly with an occlusive plastic dressing at all times
Give full tub baths daily until the stump falls off

rationales.A: Correct. MedlinePlus/OpenStax: keep stump clean (gauze and water) and dry; fold diaper down; sponge bathe / no tub bath until stump falls off; let it fall off naturally—do not pull.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Pulling can cause bleeding; allow natural separation.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Stump should be kept dry and exposed to air; not sealed in plastic.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Avoid tub baths until the stump has fallen off.

items.topic: Motivational interviewing — open questions and reflective listening rather than confrontation
items.stem: A client who drinks heavily says, "I know I should cut down, but I'm not ready to quit." Which nurse response best reflects motivational interviewing?

options.text: Use an open question and reflective listening, such as, "Tell me more about what cutting down would mean for you," then reflect the client's ambivalence
"You are in denial. Quit immediately or you will die."
"Why haven't you already stopped if you know it is a problem?"
Argue until the client agrees that total abstinence tonight is the only acceptable plan

rationales.A: Correct. SAMHSA TIP 35: MI core skills (OARS) include open questions and reflective listening to explore ambivalence. Merck: counseling approaches include motivational enhancement therapy as psychotherapy for substance use disorders.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Confrontation and scare tactics increase discord and are not MI style.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Accusatory why questions provoke defensiveness.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Arguing for change against ambivalence violates MI spirit.

items.topic: NGN bowtie — ambivalence about cutting alcohol: MI engagement; monitor safety/withdrawal cues
items.stem: A client who drinks daily says, "Part of me wants to cut down, but drinking helps me sleep." Complete the bowtie: the priority condition, two priority actions, and two parameters to monitor.

conditions.text: Ambivalence about reducing alcohol use (change-talk mixed with sustain-talk)
Acute ischemic stroke without focal neurologic cues

actions.text: Engage with open questions and reflective listening (MI/OARS style)
Support exploration of the client's own reasons for change without shaming
Yell that the client is weak and force an immediate abstinence vow
Refuse all conversation until the client promises lifelong sobriety today
Mock the client for needing alcohol to sleep

parameters.text: Willingness to continue dialogue and any change goals the client states
Safety cues related to heavy use (withdrawal risk, intoxication, self-harm)

rationales.K1: Correct. Mixed desire to cut down vs continue use is classic ambivalence—central to MI.
rationales.A1: Correct. OARS open questions/reflective listening engage ambivalent clients.
rationales.A2: Correct. MI evokes the client's own reasons for change; avoids shame.
rationales.A5: Incorrect. Mocking is nontherapeutic and stigmatizing.
rationales.P1: Correct. Track engagement and client-stated goals.
rationales.P2: Correct. Heavy daily drinking warrants monitoring for withdrawal/intoxication/safety while counseling proceeds.
